pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📐 **Strand 3 — Geometry And Measurement**
Shape, space, measurement, position and movement — the mathematics of the world around us.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.3.1)
- B7.3.1.1 — Demonstrate understanding of angles, including adjacent, vertically opposite, complementary and supplementary angles, and use them to solve problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- measure, draw and classify angles as acute, right, obtuse, straight or reflex
- use the facts that complementary angles add up to 90° and supplementary angles add up to 180°
- identify adjacent and vertically opposite angles
- use angle facts to find unknown angles

pages.title: Measuring and classifying angles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Measure and classify angles according to their measured sizes — right, acute, obtuse and reflex.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.1.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Angle** — An **angle** is the amount of turn between two arms that meet at a point called the **vertex**. Angles are measured in **degrees (°)**. A full turn is 360°.
[[fig:m7-f32|Figure 8.1: Types of angles]]
| **Type** | **Size** |
|---|---|
| Acute angle | greater than 0° and less than 90° |
| Right angle | exactly 90° |
| Obtuse angle | greater than 90° and less than 180° |
| Straight angle | exactly 180° |
| Reflex angle | greater than 180° and less than 360° |
## Using a protractor
[[fig:m7-f33|Figure 8.2: Measuring ∠ABC = 50° with a protractor]]
1. Place the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex.
2. Line up the base line (0°) with one arm of the angle.
3. Read the scale that starts at 0° on that arm, where the other arm crosses it.
To **draw** an angle of, say, 120°: draw one arm, place the protractor on its end point, mark 120° on the scale starting from 0°, and join the mark to the end point.
To draw a **reflex** angle such as 300°, draw 360° − 300° = 60° and mark the reflex angle on the outside.
## ✏️ Example 8.1
Classify each angle: a) 47° b) 90° c) 135° d) 210° e) 180° f) 359°
**Solution**
a) acute b) right c) obtuse d) reflex e) straight f) reflex

pages.title: Keep going
pages.body:
> 🧪 **Activity 8.1 — Angle hunt and angle drawing**
1. Your teacher will give you a worksheet of angles (not drawn to scale). Estimate each angle first, then measure it with a protractor and sort the angles into acute, right, obtuse and reflex.
2. Draw angles of 30°, 45°, 60°, 75°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 270° and 300°. Exchange your drawings with a partner who measures them to check your accuracy (within 1°).
3. Find angles in the classroom: the corner of a book, the hands of a clock at 2 o'clock, an open door. Classify each one.

pages.title: Complementary and supplementary angles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Apply the fact that (i) complementary angles are two angles that have a sum of 90°, and (ii) supplementary angles are two angles that have a sum of 180°, to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Complementary and supplementary angles** — Two angles are **complementary** if they add up to **90°**. Two angles are **supplementary** if they add up to **180°**. (The complement of 35° is 55°; the supplement of 35° is 145°.)
[[fig:m7-f34|Figure 8.3: Find the angles marked x]]
## ✏️ Example 8.2
Determine the missing angle marked x in each diagram above.
**Solution**
a) The two angles make a right angle: x + 35° = 90° ⟹ **x = 55°**
b) The two angles lie on a straight line: x + 128° = 180° ⟹ **x = 52°**

pages.title: Adjacent and vertically opposite angles
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Use adjacent, supplementary and vertically opposite angles to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B7.3.1.1.3
> 🔑 **Key idea: Adjacent and vertically opposite angles** — **Adjacent angles** share a vertex and a common arm and do not overlap. Adjacent angles on a straight line add up to **180°**. Angles at a point add up to **360°**. When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are called **vertically opposite angles** and they are **equal**.
[[fig:m7-f35|Figure 8.4: a = c and b = d (vertically opposite); a + b = 180° (adjacent on a straight line)]]
## ✏️ Example 8.3
Find the angles marked with letters.
[[fig:m7-f36]]
Figure 8.5: Find the angles marked with letters
**Solution**
a) Angles on a straight line: a + 47° + 68° = 180° ⟹ **a = 65°**
b) Vertically opposite: **p = 110°**. Adjacent on a straight line: q = 180° − 110° = **70°**, and r = q = **70°** (vertically opposite).
c) Angles at a point: m + 140° + 95° + 60° = 360° ⟹ **m = 65°**
## ✏️ Example 8.4
Identify each pair of angles as adjacent, vertically opposite, complementary or supplementary.
[[fig:m7-f37]]
Figure 8.6: Lines AC and BD cross at G; GE is perpendicular to AC
a) ∠AGB and ∠CGD b) ∠BGC and ∠AGD c) ∠AGB and ∠BGE d) ∠AGB and ∠BGC
**Solution**
a) **Vertically opposite** (both 50°) — they are the two acute vertical angles.
b) **Vertically opposite** (both 130°) — they are the two obtuse vertical angles.
c) **Adjacent and complementary**: 50° + 40° = 90°.
d) **Adjacent and supplementary**: 50° + 130° = 180°. So ∠AGB is supplementary to ∠BGC (and so is ∠CGD).

pages.title: Example 8.5
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 8.5
Use angle facts to find the unknowns.
[[fig:m7-f38]]
Figure 8.7: Use the angle facts
**Solution**
a) Angles on a straight line: 2x + 3x + x = 180° ⟹ 6x = 180° ⟹ **x = 30°** (the angles are 60°, 90° and 30°).
b) Vertically opposite angles are equal: 3y + 10 = 85 ⟹ 3y = 75 ⟹ **y = 25°**. The adjacent angle z = 180° − 85° = **95°**.
> 🎯 **BECE tip** Always give a **reason** for each step in angle problems, e.g. "(angles on a straight line)", "(vertically opposite angles)". Examiners award marks for reasons.

pages.title: Chapter 8 summary
pages.body:
- Acute < 90° < obtuse < 180° < reflex < 360°; right = 90°; straight = 180°.
- Complementary angles sum to 90°; supplementary angles sum to 180°.
- Angles on a straight line sum to 180°; angles at a point sum to 360°.
- Vertically opposite angles are equal.

Is it possible for two obtuse angles to be supplementary? Explain.

parts.a: No. Two obtuse angles add up to more than 180°.
